dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a measure mu, real-valued function X, one of four formulation indices, and a real constant K, this predicate selects the formulation indexed by that constructor: D011 for D010, D004 for D008, D003 for D007, and D005 for D009.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the central indexed property converted by the target from every input formulation i with constant Ki to every output formulation j with constant Kj.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: A four-element inductive index type, with the four nullary constructors D010, D008, D007, and D009 as confirmed by its recursor.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The universal binders i and j range independently over the four formulations, so the assertion includes all sixteen ordered conversions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: The absolute-exponential-moment formulation at K: X is measurable, K is positive, and for every real lambda with 0 <= lambda <= 1/K, exp(lambda*|X|) is mu-integrable and its integral is at most exp(K*lambda).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the formulation selected by index D007 and is both a possible antecedent and a possible requested conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: The moment-growth formulation at K: X is measurable, K is positive, and D012 holds, namely for every real p >= 1 the real power |X|^p is integrable and has integral at most (K*p)^p (with an additional almost-everywhere measurability requirement in D012).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the formulation selected by index D008 and is one member of the universally interconvertible family.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: The single exponential-moment formulation at K: X is measurable, K is positive, exp(|X|/K) is mu-integrable, and its integral is at most 2.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the formulation selected by index D009 and is one member of the universally interconvertible family.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: A four-way dependent case eliminator for the index type, implemented using D013 after evaluating each Unit-thunk.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes LocalDef001 select exactly one of its four property predicates according to its index.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: The nullary index constructor selecting the D003 absolute-exponential-moment formulation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Taking i or j equal to this constructor makes LocalDef001 mean D003.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: The nullary index constructor selecting the D004 moment-growth formulation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Taking i or j equal to this constructor makes LocalDef001 mean D004.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: The nullary index constructor selecting the D005 single exponential-moment formulation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Taking i or j equal to this constructor makes LocalDef001 mean D005.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: The nullary index constructor selecting the D011 exponential-tail formulation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Taking i or j equal to this constructor makes LocalDef001 mean D011.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: The exponential-tail formulation at K: X is measurable, K is positive, and for every real t >= 0, mu({omega : |X(omega)| >= t}), converted to a real, is at most 2*exp(-t/K).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the formulation selected by index D010 and is both a possible antecedent and a possible requested conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: X is almost-everywhere measurable with respect to mu and, for every real p >= 1, the function |X|^p (real exponentiation) is mu-integrable and its integral is at most (K*p)^p.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013

binders: There exists a real constant C, chosen once and independently of every probability space, random variable, formulation pair, and input scale.

Universally quantify over every type Omega with a measurable-space structure, every measure mu on Omega carrying an IsProbabilityMeasure instance, every function X : Omega -> Real, every ordered pair i,j of the four formulation indices, and every real Ki.
After all of those choices and the antecedent proofs, existentially choose a real Kj; thus Kj may depend on Omega, mu, X, i, j, Ki, and the proofs, while C may not.
hypotheses: The measure mu is a probability measure.
The input scale Ki is strictly positive.

X satisfies the indexed property LocalDef001(mu,X,i,Ki): according to i this is the exponential-tail, moment-growth, small-parameter absolute-exponential-moment, or single exponential-moment condition described below.
conclusions: There exists a strictly positive real scale Kj satisfying Kj <= C*Ki.
At that scale Kj, X satisfies LocalDef001(mu,X,j,Kj), i.e. the formulation selected by j.
Consequently, the same universal factor C converts any one of the four formulations into any other one on every real-valued random variable over every probability space.
mathematical_definitions: Tail formulation T(K): X is measurable, K>0, and for every t>=0, mu{|X|>=t} <= 2 exp(-t/K).
Moment formulation M(K): X is measurable, K>0, X is also a.e. measurable, and for every real p>=1, |X|^p is integrable and integral |X|^p dmu <= (Kp)^p; powers are real powers.
Small-parameter absolute-MGF formulation A(K): X is measurable, K>0, and for every real lambda in [0,1/K], exp(lambda|X|) is integrable and integral exp(lambda|X|) dmu <= exp(K lambda).
Single exponential-moment formulation E(K): X is measurable, K>0, exp(|X|/K) is integrable, and integral exp(|X|/K) dmu <= 2.
The four index constructors select T, M, A, and E respectively as D010, D008, D007, and D009.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal real constant C at least 1 such that, on every probability space and for every real-valued function X, each of four specified exponential-tail, moment-growth, absolute-exponential-moment, and single exponential-moment formulations implies every other formulation after replacing its positive scale Ki by some positive scale Kj no larger than C times Ki. The same C works simultaneously for all spaces, measures, functions, ordered pairs of formulations, and input scales.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement is restricted to real-valued functions on probability spaces; it says nothing about non-probability finite measures or vector-valued functions.

All four formulations explicitly include ordinary measurability of X and positivity of their scale. The target's separate Ki>0 and Kj>0 conditions therefore duplicate conditions already present in the indexed predicates.
The moment formulation quantifies over real p>=1 and uses Real.rpow, not merely integer moments; its stated inequality is for the raw integral and is not syntactically written as an Lp-norm bound.
The small-parameter exponential formulation concerns exp(lambda*|X|), not exp(lambda*X), and only nonnegative lambda up to 1/K.

The tail event uses |X|>=t (including equality), and its measure is converted from an extended nonnegative real to a real; probability-measure finiteness prevents the infinity-to-real conversion from becoming pathological here.
The proposition gives no numerical value, optimality, or minimality for C or Kj, and does not assert that Kj equals C*Ki.
No centering, mean-zero condition, independence assumption, or symmetry of X is encoded.
There is no evident vacuity from impossible indexed premises: for example, the zero function satisfies each formulation for every positive scale on a probability space.
